patient.name: Maya Chen
patient.chiefComplaint: Nausea, vomiting, and rapid breathing for the past day

history.hpi: Roommate found the patient breathing rapidly and unusually thirsty this morning after two days of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Patient reports her insulin pump alarm has been going off intermittently over the past two days and she is unsure whether it has been delivering insulin correctly. She endorses excessive thirst and frequent urination over that time and has been unable to keep fluids down since yesterday evening.
pastMedical: Type 1 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed at age 9
medications: Insulin pump (rapid-acting insulin lispro) — possible malfunction over past 2 days
history.lastOralIntake: Sips of water this morning; vomited twice overnight; no solid food in over 24 hours
history.events: Roommate called 911 after finding the patient breathing rapidly and confused about the day of the week

scene.dispatch: 22-year-old female, nausea and rapid breathing, residence
scene.location: Second-floor apartment bedroom, patient sitting upright on the edge of the bed
scene.bystanders: Roommate present, called 911, reports patient has been unwell for two days
visualCues: Insulin pump visible on abdomen with tubing that appears kinked
Emesis basin nearby with small amount of clear vomitus

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 22-year-old female with known type 1 diabetes sitting upright, breathing deeply and rapidly, with a fruity odor to her breath and signs of dehydration.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Kussmaul respirations — deep and rapid, RR 30, lungs clear bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present but weak, tachycardic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all extremities, mild generalized weakness
otherFindings: Diffuse mild abdominal tenderness without rigidity
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I just feel so sick and thirsty, I can't stop breathing like this."

expectedActions.rationale: Confirms hyperglycemia and guides fluid resuscitation decisions.

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess for dehydration: sunken eyes, dry mucous membranes, tachypnea, tachycardia
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Secondary survey pertinent to altered blood glucose level: Constitutional: assess for tachycardia, hypotension, and tachypnea Eyes: assess for sunken eyes from dehydration Nose/mouth/ears: assess for dry mucous membranes or tongue bite from seizure
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms the severity of dehydration driving fluid resuscitation decisions.

expectedActions.shortAction: Obtain 12-lead EKG to screen for hyperkalemic changes or ischemia
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Obtain 12-lead EKG to assess for findings consistent with hyperkalemia or acute coronary syndrome
expectedActions.rationale: DKA can cause dangerous potassium shifts that manifest on the EKG before lab results are available.

expectedActions.shortAction: Normal saline bolus 1,300 mL IV (65 kg × 20 mL/kg = 1,300 mL) infused at 1,000 mL/hr
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Provide volume expansion with normal saline bolus Adult: Normal saline 20 mL/kg at rate of 1000 mL/hr; if symptoms of hypovolemic shock, follow Shock Guideline.
expectedActions.rationale: Profound dehydration from osmotic diuresis is a hallmark of DKA and drives most of the early morbidity.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs, mental status, and dehydration signs after fluid bolus
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Reassess patient Reassess vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment), mental status, and signs of dehydration
expectedActions.rationale: Overly aggressive fluid administration without reassessment risks cerebral edema, so response must be tracked closely.

transitions.condition: Crew recognizes Kussmaul respirations, fruity breath, and dehydration in a known type 1 diabetic, checks point-of-care glucose, obtains a 12-lead, and begins weight-based fluid resuscitation per the Hyperglycemia guideline.

The crew infuses the fluid bolus but does not reassess vital signs or mental status afterward; over the following minutes the patient's mental status paradoxically declines rather than improves, raising concern for cerebral edema.

phases.name: BGL checked, fluids started
phases.description: Point-of-care glucose confirms severe hyperglycemia. Crew obtains a 12-lead to screen for hyperkalemic changes or ischemia and initiates a weight-based normal saline bolus for dehydration.
phases.triggerCondition: After recognizing Kussmaul respirations, fruity breath, and dehydration in a known type 1 diabetic, the crew checks blood glucose, obtains a 12-lead, and begins fluid resuscitation per the Hyperglycemia guideline.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, tachycardic, IV access established
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all extremities, mild generalized weakness
otherFindings: 12-lead shows sinus tachycardia, no peaked T waves or ischemic changes
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Is that going to help? I really don't feel good."

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport to closest appropriate receiving facility
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Disposition Transport to closest appropriate receiving facility
expectedActions.rationale: DKA requires hospital-based insulin therapy and lab monitoring that cannot be completed in the field.

transitions.condition: After the normal saline bolus infuses, the crew reassesses vital signs, mental status, and signs of dehydration; the patient shows improved perfusion and a clearing sensorium.

phases.name: Reassessed after fluid bolus
phases.description: Serial reassessment after the fluid bolus shows improving perfusion, a clearing sensorium, and easing respiratory distress. Patient is packaged for transport.
phases.triggerCondition: After the normal saline bolus infuses, the crew reassesses vital signs, mental status, and signs of dehydration; the patient shows improved perfusion and a clearing sensorium.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: RR 20, less labored, Kussmaul pattern easing
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel a little better, still really thirsty though."

phases.name: Fluids given without reassessment
phases.description: The fluid bolus was infused but the crew did not reassess vital signs or mental status afterward. The patient's mental status is declining rather than improving, with a widening pulse pressure and irregular respirations concerning for cerebral edema.
phases.triggerCondition: The crew infuses the fluid bolus but does not reassess vital signs or mental status afterward; over the following minutes the patient's mental status paradoxically declines rather than improves, raising concern for cerebral edema from rapid fluid shifts.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent but breathing pattern increasingly irregular
clinicalPresentation.breathing: RR 14, irregular, no longer following the Kussmaul pattern
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Pulses full and bounding, relatively bradycardic for illness severity

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize declining mental status as possible cerebral edema; stop IV fluids and elevate head of bed
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Closely monitor for signs of altered mental status, increased intracranial pressure, and immediately discontinue IV fluids and elevate head of bed if signs of increased ICP develop
expectedActions.rationale: Bradycardia, widening pulse pressure, and irregular respirations after fluid administration suggest evolving cerebral edema, a leading cause of death in DKA.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess and manage airway as needed given declining mental status
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Reassess and manage airway as needed
expectedActions.rationale: Declining mental status threatens airway protection and warrants close reassessment.
